Chicago Lawn counts 19,137 housing units with a median build year of 1951. 75.4 percent predate 1970 and 38.6 percent predate 1940. The published buckets stop at 1970, so the pre-1978 share is higher than 75.4 percent by an amount nobody publishes and this page will not guess at.

Owner households here number 9,369 and renter households 8,224, a 53.3 percent owner-occupied place. The stock behind those households is 44.6 percent detached, 2.1 percent attached and 52.9 percent multi-unit, at a median of 5.8 rooms. Median value across that stock is $224,494.

Against the other 22 Chicago community areas covered here, Chicago Lawn sits in the top four for the largest housing stock overall (19,137 units) and the largest owner-occupied market (9,369 households).

Where Chicago Lawn departs most from the 76 place average: prewar housing at 38.6 percent against a 15.8 percent average, housing in buildings of two or more at 52.9 percent against a 29 percent average and townhomes and rowhouses at 2.1 percent against a 7.5 percent average.

Source: Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning, Community Data Snapshots 2026, drawing on American Community Survey 2024 estimates. Every dollar figure on this page is a published Census estimate of what homes in the area are worth. None of it is a price for work.

Why two houses in Chicago Lawn do not price the same

With 38.6 percent of Chicago Lawn prewar and a 1951 median, the ceilings are the part people forget. Old plaster ceilings move, they have usually been patched at least once, and a flat white over the top of that shows every previous repair the moment the light comes across it. They are worth pricing as their own line. 52.9 percent of the housing sits in buildings of two units or more, which means hallways, stairwells and unit turnarounds are as much of the work as living rooms. Those get quoted per unit and they get done to a date.

The lines a quote for Chicago Lawn needs to show

  • Containment, not just paint. 75.4 percent of housing in Chicago Lawn was built before 1970, so on most addresses here the lead-safe setup and the cleanup are part of the job and part of the hours.
  • Plaster as well as drywall. 38.6 percent of Chicago Lawn is prewar. Plaster cracks along the lath and comes back if it is only filled, so wall repair is a different line from wall painting.
  • Per unit, to a date. 52.9 percent of units here are in buildings of two or more. Turnover work is priced per unit and scheduled to a move-out, not to the weather.
  • Two different customers. 53.3 percent owner occupancy means homeowner work and landlord work sit side by side here, and they want opposite things from a schedule.

What the housing here is likely made of

Most of it is postwar masonry with a heavy share of two-flats and small apartment buildings. Trim, soffit, porches and common areas are where the exterior paint in Chicago Lawn actually is, and unit turnover sits alongside homeowner work.

It is read off exactly two things: the 1951 median build year, and the split between 44.6 percent detached houses, 2.1 percent attached homes and 52.9 percent in buildings of two units or more.

Inference, and worth saying so. Wall material in Chicago Lawn is not in the Census tables or the regional data, which is why that sentence carries no number when everything else here does.

Chicago Lawn is mostly pre-1978 stock, and that changes the setup

75.4 percent of housing units were built before 1970, and the community-area data does not publish a 1978 bucket, so the real pre-1978 share is higher than that by an amount nobody has measured in Chicago Lawn. Anything built before 1978 sits inside the federal Renovation, Repair and Painting rule the moment work disturbs its paint. Illinois never took the program on, so the agency behind it here is EPA itself.

What it changes is the front and the back of a Chicago Lawn job, not the middle: plastic and sealed openings before, a specific cleanup standard after. It starts at roughly six square feet of disturbed paint per room inside, twenty square feet outside, and always on window replacement.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Chicago Lawn.

Ask about it early. It changes the sequence of a job rather than the price of the paint, and a contractor who has thought about it will tell you in plain terms what happens on day one.

No lead-safe certification is claimed anywhere on this site, because no number has been provided to put here. The panel below leaves the slot open on purpose, in Chicago Lawn and everywhere else. Ask any contractor for theirs.

Questions

Asked about Chicago Lawn

My house in Chicago Lawn is plaster, not drywall. Is that a problem?

It is not a problem, it is a different repair. Plaster cracks along the lath and comes back if it is only filled, so the fix has to address the movement rather than the line. With a 1951 median build year most of Chicago Lawn is plaster over lath on at least some walls and ceilings. Say so when you call, because it changes the time estimate and it is better said before the quote than after.

How quickly can somebody look at it?

Chicago Lawn is 5.9 straight-line miles from the shop, which is close enough that looking at the work and doing the work do not have to be the same trip. That matters most on small jobs, because a repair that is worth doing gets seen instead of being pushed into a bigger job later. Call 708-935-4289.

Is the $224,494 median home value in Chicago Lawn what a job here costs?

No. That figure describes the houses, not the work. $224,494 is what the Census estimates a home in Chicago Lawn is worth, and it earns its place on this page because value tracks size and age, which is what a painter is actually pricing. There is no price list on this site because there is no honest local one to publish yet.

Who actually shows up in Chicago Lawn?

Our painters do the work and the owner runs the job, so the person who priced it is still the person answerable for it. Call 708-935-4289, say where in Chicago Lawn you are and what needs doing, and you will get an answer rather than a callback from an office.
